anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Stale, incomplete, or missing optimizer statistics misrepresent actual data distribution and drive systematic cardinality misestimation.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume or request more CPU cycles than the host can provide, leading to sustained CPU saturation and broad latency inflation.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Database processes exceed kernel-enforced quotas for threads, file handles, shared-memory segments, or similar objects, causing allocation failures outside the engine’s direct control.

When these three root causes strike simultaneously, the system exhibits a compound failure pattern: execution plans generated from bad statistics choose CPU-intensive operators (e.g., hash joins, large sort/aggregate, over-parallelized scans) that flood all cores. The surge of threads, processes, and I/O descriptors needed to execute those plans pushes the database past OS limits, producing sporadic errors such as "cannot create thread", "too many open files", or "failed to allocate shared memory". Meanwhile, CPU saturation lengthens query runtimes, further extending the interval during which OS quotas remain exhausted. Users observe a mix of symptoms—wildly inaccurate plan estimates, skyrocketing CPU wait and run-queue times, sudden session or worker spawn failures, and cascading slowdowns across unrelated queries.

Causal chain: stale or absent statistics misguide the optimizer into selecting plans that require excessive CPU and high degrees of parallelism; this overconsumption pushes the host into CPU saturation. The inflated worker and descriptor counts generated by those plans rapidly consume kernel-limited resources, which in turn block new sessions, background statistics refresh jobs, and parallel workers—preventing automatic statistics collection and perpetuating the original misestimation. Each anomaly therefore reinforces the others, producing a feedback loop that degrades throughput, increases error rates, and risks partial or complete service outage.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with Bad handshake.
entry.trigger_condition: A client does not complete the initial connection packet exchange within connect_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The connection attempt fails during handshake.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
